page: Amazon Web Services c6in.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs based on 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations show strong performance in specific vector and cryptographic operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench ray tracing score of 49,893.0 and an image processing score of 15,221.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Passmark CPU encryption tests also registered in the top 25% with a score of 43,676.13, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES. Most other compute metrics, such as the Passmark CPU score of 48,648.63 and the Geekbench multi-core score of 15,824.0, fall within the average range.

With a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps, this instance is designed for network-intensive workloads. Memory read-only bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 2,506.71 GB/sec, while uncached large block reads operate at 163.17 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds for prompt processing reach 2,446.12 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, though text generation on larger 70B models drops to 2.82 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is suited for network-optimized compute tasks, cryptographic processing, and distributed compilation workloads.
